The left-hand side involves the canonical isomorphism from the image constructed via the image factorization to the image constructed via the kernel of the cokernel. The right-hand side is the kernel inclusion of the cokernel projection. This equality is a standard property in abelian categories relating the two constructions of the image.

The `simp` tactic can close this goal because the lemma `CategoryTheory.Abelian.imageIsoImage_hom_comp_image_ι` (or a similar lemma) is in the simp set. This lemma states exactly that `(imageIsoImage f).hom ≫ Limits.image.ι f = kernel.ι (cokernel.π f)`. Since the goal matches the lemma's conclusion, `simp` will apply the lemma and simplify the goal to `True`.

The lemma `CategoryTheory.Limits.IsImage.lift_ι` states that for an `IsImage` instance `hF` on a mono factorisation `F`, we have `hF.lift (Image.monoFactorisation f) ≫ image.ι f = F.m`. Here `F.m` is the monomorphism part of the factorisation. In the abelian category setting, the image factorisation `imageStrongEpiMonoFactorisation_m` provides a mono factorisation `F` where `F.m` is exactly `kernel.ι (cokernel.π f)`. Therefore, applying `hF.lift (Image.monoFactorisation f) ≫ image.ι f = F.m` with `hF` being the `IsImage` instance for `imageStrongEpiMonoFactorisation_m` directly gives the desired equality, because `(imageIsoImage f).hom` is defined as `hF.lift (Image.monoFactorisation f)`. The `simp` tactic will use the `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]` annotation on `IsImage.lift_ι` to rewrite the left-hand side to the right-hand side, closing the goal.
